stages.label: Absent
stages.desc: Nothing of the kind exists, and a dated source says so.

stages.label: Preparing
stages.desc: Announced, drafted, piloted: an intention with an instrument or a pilot behind it.

stages.label: Establishing
stages.desc: In service, but limited in scope, coverage or use.

stages.label: Operating
stages.desc: In service at scale: funded, regulated, used, maintained.

stages.label: Leading
stages.desc: Embedded: interoperable, measured, sustained; at or beyond the continental norm.

grey.label: No evidence
grey.desc: Not staged: nothing held, or evidence held that meets no rung.

digital.rural--digitalisation-of-rural-h.label: Digitalisation of rural health clinics: HMIS

ladder.text: A dated source states that routine health reporting is not entered digitally at any level of the health system.

A digital reporting system is used by hospitals only or in some districts, or a national rollout is contracted or being prepared: staff trained, equipment delivered or an agreement signed. Primary clinics do not use it, beyond pilot sites.
A national system takes the clinics' reports, which are keyed in at district level from the clinics' paper forms. A minority of primary clinics enter their own reports, or no figure is published.
More than half of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility. The figure is a published share, or a count given with its total.
At least 90 per cent of primary clinics enter their own reports at the facility, on a figure published within the past two years. Reporting completeness is published as well.

digital.rural--digitalisation-of-rural-h.label: Digitalisation of rural health clinics: EMR

ladder.text: A dated source states that patient records are kept on paper at every level of the health system.

Electronic patient records are in use in some hospitals or pilot facilities, or a national system is procured or being prepared: staff trained, equipment delivered or an agreement signed. Primary clinics do not use them, beyond pilot sites.

Electronic patient records are in use in most hospitals, or in primary clinics in some districts, but each record stays in the facility that made it. A minority of primary clinics use them, or no figure is published.
More than half of primary clinics keep electronic patient records, entered at the point of care. Each record is held under a unique patient identifier and can be retrieved at another facility.
At least 90 per cent of primary clinics keep such shared records, on a figure published within the past two years. A record can be retrieved anywhere in the public network.

digital.rural--digitalisation-of-rural-r.label: Digitalisation of rural registry offices: civil registration

ladder.text: A dated source states that local civil registration offices register births and deaths on paper only. Scanning or keying old registers does not change this.
A system for local offices to register births digitally is being prepared or piloted, or one runs at the national office or in the capital only.

Births are entered digitally when they are registered, past any pilot, in some local offices; they are a minority, or no share of offices is published. A share of offices equipped or connected, however high, places here.
More than half of local offices enter births digitally at the office when they are registered, into the national register. The figure is a published share, or a count given with its total.
At least 90 per cent of local offices do so, for deaths as well as births, on a figure published within the past two years. The figure gives the share for rural offices.

digital.rural--digitalisation-of-rural-p.label: Digitalisation of rural primary schools: EMIS

ladder.text: A dated source states that primary schools keep their learners' records on paper only. An annual school census, however it is collected and whatever it is called, does not change this.
An EMIS for primary schools is being prepared or piloted: staff trained, equipment delivered, an agreement signed or pilot schools using it. Or one runs in secondary schools only.

An EMIS is past its pilot and in live use in some primary schools, which enter attendance or results during the year; they are a minority, or no figure is published. Or schools past the pilot fill a national learner register once a year.
More than half of primary schools enter attendance or results for each learner during the school year, at the school. The figure is a published share, or a count given with its total.
At least 90 per cent of primary schools do so, with attendance entered daily, on a figure published within the past two years. The figure gives the share for rural schools.

AGO.short: Clinics report on paper, and municipal or provincial offices enter the figures into the national reporting system (2025).
AGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's Office of Studies, Planning and Statistics, GEPE, oversees the health information system and has been moving it onto DHIS2 since 2015, as an article of June 2025 states. WHO supported the drafting in 2024 of a strategic plan for the system running to 2030, and the European Union finances that plan's preparation. The World Bank's appraisal of 4 November 2025 proposes US$5 million to extend DHIS2's functions and geographic coverage.

Tiers in use. A technical mission in March 2026 found the DHIS2-based national system had more than 4,700 registered users.

Where data is digitised. Health facilities collect and report their data on paper, and the figures are aggregated and entered into DHIS2 at municipal or provincial level, as the June 2025 article states.

Last twelve months. In March 2026 a joint WHO Angola and HISP UiO mission with Saudigitus assessed the platform, and the ministry and its partners agreed to upgrade it, harmonise data across information flows, build dashboards for decision-makers and train staff at all levels.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Health facilities report in paper format, and entry into DHIS2 is made at municipal or provincial level, on the June 2025 article's account.

Not held. No source names the tiers using the system, and no count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published. The strategic plan is not reported as adopted, and no domestic budget line is tied to the system by name.

BDI.short: Health centres enter their own reports into the national reporting system (2023), but no figure shows how many of them do.
BDI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's Direction du Système National d'Information Sanitaire manages the health information system, and its IT cell administers DHIS2, as the ministry's statistical yearbook of July 2024 states. In a memorandum signed with the United States on 6 February 2026 the government commits to use DHIS2 as its national health data warehouse, and the United States plans $188,526 for it in 2026.

Tiers in use. The ministry collected its 2023 data through the national DHIS2 platform from health centres, district hospitals and national hospitals, with report forms set for the community, the health centre and the hospital.

Where data is digitised. Facilities record by hand in paper registers and the entry into DHIS2 is made at the facility, by the deputy head of a health centre and by a hospital's information officer, the World Bank reported in March 2023. Community health workers' monthly reports go to the health centre for entry, by the method note of the ministry's 2023 yearbook.

Last twelve months. The memorandum of 6 February 2026 runs to 31 December 2030 and costs United States support for DHIS2 at about $609,872 over the term, for linking it with SIDAinfo and other systems and for bringing in supply chain and laboratory data.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Reports in DHIS2 were more than 95% complete for health centres at 30 June 2022, in the World Bank's assessment of March 2023.

Not held. No share or count of health centres keying their own reports, with a denominator, is published, and nothing on the point is dated inside the last three years. The one community application described as interfaced with DHIS2 was still in test in 2023.

BEN.short: Health zone offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system in 2022; how many clinics enter their own is not published.
BEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's 2022 statistical yearbook says the ministry adopted DHIS2 from 2014 as its platform for managing health data, under what it calls the Système National d'Information et de Gestion Sanitaires (SNIGS). The ministry's programme budget for 2024-2026 puts its Direction des Systèmes d'Information in charge of the information systems action and funds that action from domestic resources alone, at 590,406,313 FCFA in 2024. The same document sets targets of 80 per cent in 2024 and 85 per cent in 2025 and 2026 for health facilities whose statistics are integrated in SNIGS.

Tiers in use. In 2019 SNIGS collected a monthly return from health centres and another from hospitals, on standard paper forms, and reported indicators for the national teaching hospital.

Where data is digitised. In 2022 a facility sent its paper report to the zone sanitaire before the 5th of each month and the zone keyed it into DHIS2 before the 20th, in every zone sanitaire. Certain equipped facilities and community relays keyed their own monthly forms directly into the data warehouse.

Last twelve months. The programme budget of December 2023 allocates the information systems action the same 590,406,313 FCFA in 2026 as in 2024 and 2025.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. Abt Global, in November 2023, names one private facility, the Minonkpo Clinic in Cotonou, as recording its data directly into DHIS2 since 2020, against 752 private health facilities in the country.

Not held. No number or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and no tier below the health centre is named. No dated event falls in the last twelve months.

BFA.short: Clinics and hospitals reported into the national system in 2024, entered at district or facility; the share of clinics entering their own is not published.
BFA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's Direction générale des études et des statistiques sectorielles coordinates the national health information system, under its procedures manual of July 2023. Enabel reported in July 2026 that a strategic plan for the system for 2026-2030 is being implemented. The ministry's digital health strategy of January 2025 is costed at 42.6 billion FCFA, against 2.8 billion FCFA of available funds.

Tiers in use. In 2024 Endos-BF, the ministry's name for its health data warehouse, took the monthly activity reports of public and private health facilities and of the units of the regional and university hospitals. The Countdown to 2030 country team states that 83% of expected monthly facility reports were received nationally through DHIS2 in 2024.

Where data is digitised. In 2024 health facilities sent their monthly reports to the district, where data managers keyed them into Endos-BF. The ministry's strategy of January 2025 lists the scaling-up of decentralised entry of routine data in health facilities among the health system's innovations.

Last twelve months. Enabel reports that district management teams and head nurses of health posts were trained in data analysis and use, including quality control of DHIS2 data, at Dédougou and Tenkodogo in July 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. In 2024, in the health districts implementing decentralised entry, the heads of health facilities entered their own monthly activity reports. In 2021 entry by the primary health centres themselves was operational in the Boucle du Mouhoun, one of 13 regions.

Not held. No number or share of primary clinics, or of districts, keying their own monthly reports is held. Who finances the system is not stated, and no community system is shown exchanging data with Endos-BF.

BWA.short: All public health facilities reported into the national system in 2016-18; they report on paper (2025), and it is unclear where the figures are entered.
BWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. WHO's country office report for 2024-2025 describes DHIS2 as the Government's selected "gold standard" platform for aggregate data. The Ministry of Health and Wellness's roadmap, dated 2019, set one integrated DHIS2 as the default reporting system for the sector, under the ministry's stewardship.

Tiers in use. MEASURE Evaluation's country profile of August 2019 records a national deployment of DHIS2 aggregating health data from all facilities in the country.

Where data is digitised. WHO's report for 2024-2025 lists facilities' heavy reliance on paper-based reporting as a challenge and recommends revising the DHIS2 dashboards and trackers "to enable onsite data capturing".

Last twelve months. WHO's report for 2024-2025 has DHIS2 used to monitor HIV, immunisation and reproductive, maternal and child health across districts.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. MEASURE Evaluation gives 100% of public health facilities as reporting through DHIS2, for 2016 to 2018, a share of all public health facilities.

Not held. The level at which facilities' paper reports are keyed is not established, and no share or count of clinics entering their own reports is held; the 100% is of facilities reporting, and carries no numerator or denominator. No plan or financing dated within the last three years is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months.

CAF.short: The national reporting system runs in all 35 districts (2025), but only 21.4% of 14 facilities checked in 2024 entered data electronically.
CAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health and Population undertook the reform of the national health information system (SNIS) and adopted DHIS2 as the national platform, on a DHIS2 Community poster of May 2026. The ministry's immunisation recovery plan of November 2020 gives its SNIS service the administration of DHIS2. The World Bank's appraisal of May 2022 states that the SENI-Plus project will finance the transition to DHIS2 in all 35 districts.

Tiers in use. The ministry's plan of November 2020 names 5 central hospitals with data managers keying SNIS data, alongside the 35 district and 7 regional health offices.

Where data is digitised. By 2025 DHIS2 had been deployed in all 35 health districts, with data managers recruited and offline and VSAT connections. The plan of November 2020 has facilities' SNIS reports arriving at the district, where data managers key them. The IMPULSE study found a functional electronic system in 83.3% of the 6 district health offices it assessed to July 2024.

Last twelve months. Report completeness in DHIS2 rose from 52% in 2020 to more than 85% in 2025 across the 35 health districts.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The IMPULSE study found that 21.4% of the 14 facilities it assessed, hospitals and health centres in Bangui and three health regions chosen for access and security, used a functional electronic system for routine data entry, on data collected to July 2024.

Not held. No fact held shows primary clinics entering their own reports, and no national share is held; the 21.4% is of 14 facilities chosen for access and security. No plan or financing dated within the last three years is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months.

CIV.short: In 2020 departmental health offices entered clinics' paper reports into the national system; nothing more recent shows where reports are entered.
CIV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's annual report for 2020 calls DHIS2 the national database of routine data and places its checking with the ministry's own information directorate. The ministry's costed health plan for 2021 to 2025, dated October 2021, carries 30 million FCFA a year to make DHIS 2 interoperable with four other systems. USAID's President's Malaria Initiative financed support to routine reporting and the use of DHIS2 data in 20 health districts in 2022.

Tiers in use. The October 2021 plan states that DHIS 2 is deployed in all regional and departmental health directorates, all regional hospital centres and general hospitals, and in a few first-contact health establishments. In 2020 the general hospitals and regional hospital centres had their data keyed into DHIS2 by their own data managers.

Where data is digitised. In 2020 each first-contact establishment drew up a monthly report from its registers, and the district's epidemiological surveillance officer keyed those reports into DHIS2 at the departmental health directorate. PMI Measure Malaria reported for 2022 that health centres reporting on paper had no access to the information in DHIS2.

Last twelve months. On 11 September 2025 the ministry's Health Information Directorate organised a DHIS2 technical working group meeting on managing the national DHIS2 database, which it calls SIGSANTE.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. By the ministry's account for 2020, first-contact establishments did not enter their own reports. District reports reached 100% completeness and 98.23% timeliness in 2020.

Not held. Nothing held after 2022 says where clinics' reports are keyed, and nothing says the few first-contact establishments with DHIS 2 enter their own reports. No plan or financing dated within the last three years is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months.

CMR.short: The national system is in use countrywide with entry at the facility (2022 ministry plan), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so.
CMR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Public Health's digital health plan for 2026 to 2030 calls DHIS2 the ministry's national health information system, adopted in 2017, and costs work on its management plan and interoperability framework. The ministry states that under the 2020-2024 plan DHIS2 was financed through partner conventions, with no dedicated national digital health budget.

Tiers in use. The national statistics institute states that DHIS2 carries aggregate data from the monthly activity reports of all health facilities across the national territory, and used those reports for 2018 to 2022. The ministry's DHIS2 plan of April 2022 counts 197 health districts and 6,200 facilities.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's DHIS2 plan of April 2022 states that a nationwide HMIS is in place for aggregate data, with data entry at the facility level. Facilities still fill paper registers and monthly reporting booklets, which the plan budgets to reprint for 6,200 facilities.

Last twelve months. The ministry published its digital health plan for 2026 to 2030 in March 2026, with 2026 budget lines for DHIS2 deployment, maintenance, servers and interoperability.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry's family health directorate gives completeness of monthly activity reports in DHIS2 as 96% nationally for October to December 2025, and timeliness as 89%, read from DHIS2 on 23 February 2026.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 96% measures reports received in DHIS2. Use is not broken down by facility level, and nothing dated since April 2022 states where data is entered.

COD.short: Health zone offices enter facilities' paper reports into the national system (2021), which covers 75.3% of all health facilities (2022).
COD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. DHIS2.org in December 2025 calls the national DHIS2 locally owned and managed infrastructure of the Ministry of Health, in use at national scale since 2013, and names Gavi, the Global Fund and US CDC among its funders. The ministry's health informatics plan for 2020 to 2024 states that DHIS2 has been adopted as the software of its Système National d'Information Sanitaire (SNIS).

Tiers in use. The Sud-Kivu provincial health division's report of December 2021 lists paper reporting forms for health centres, health posts and general referral hospitals, and DHIS2 data sets for basic, secondary and hospital services in all 34 health zones. Nationally, the SNIS division counted 52,625 basic-services reports in DHIS2 of 53,736 expected in the second quarter of 2020.

Where data is digitised. A HISP evaluation that visited five health zones in Kinshasa and Haut-Katanga in late 2021 found that facilities send their reports on paper to the health zone office, where they are entered into DHIS2; some large facilities enter their own.

Last twelve months. In February 2026 Lualaba became the first province to make the HIV Insight Dashboard, an analysis application built inside the national DHIS2, its primary tool for provincial meetings and data validation.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Ministry of Public Health's Countdown to 2030 report, signed on 14 August 2022, states that 12,050 of the 16,010 health facilities listed in DHIS2, 75.3% of all health facilities, report in it.

Not held. No share or count of facilities entering their own reports is held, and no coverage figure dated after 2022; the 75.3% counts facilities whose reports are in DHIS2. No plan dated after 2024 is held, and the tiers are named for Sud-Kivu alone.

COG.short: All 52 health districts enter clinics' paper reports into the national system (2024); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
COG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's national health development plan for 2023 to 2026, published in September 2024, names DHIS2 as the principal platform for collecting and processing health information, within what the ministry calls the Système national d'information sanitaire (SNIS). The plan lists a health information directorate in the ministry and a database manager in every health district, and says the platform was built with Global Fund and Gavi support.

Tiers in use. The plan of September 2024 states that standard collection tools exist in health centres, district referral hospitals and private facilities, and that general hospitals' forms are configured in DHIS2 with their monthly reporting still to begin.

Where data is digitised. The same plan states that nearly all public, private and faith-based facilities compile their reports on paper and send them to the health districts for entry, all 12 departments and 52 districts having been trained on DHIS2. WHO reports data completeness of 87% and timeliness of 47.9% in 2024.

Last twelve months. WHO's annual report for 2025 says that during the year, with its support, 401 data collectors were equipped for electronic transmission of data and the national list of health indicators was drawn up.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The plan of September 2024 states that facilities produce their reports on paper and the health districts key them into DHIS2, and that paper collection tools remain much used while the computer tools provided are not often used.

Not held. No count or share of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and nothing on health posts. The tier, total number and software of the 401 data collectors equipped in 2025 are not stated, and no domestic budget line for the system is named.

COM.short: The national reporting system reached all 91 public health facilities (WHO, 2025), but it is not known where their reports are entered.
COM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's digital health strategy for 2022 to 2026, dated July 2021, puts the deployment of DHIS2 under its Direction de l'Information et des Statistiques Sanitaires. It schedules the extension of the national health information system with DHIS2 for January 2022 to December 2025 at US$0.60 million, all of it set against technical and financial partners. The World Bank reported in November 2024 that DHIS2 was deployed under an IDA-financed project implemented by the ministry.

Tiers in use. WHO Comoros reports that DHIS2 was extended to all 91 public-level health structures in 2025, which it calls a national extension.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's strategy of July 2021 describes the national health information system, then on GESIS, as semi-electronic and computerised at the level of the regions, with data passing from districts to regions by hand or by e-mail.

Last twelve months. During 2025, with WHO support, validation rules were put into DHIS2, a data quality self-assessment was run and a manual of standard data-management procedures was written.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. DHIS2 states that almost 99% of all public health facilities used DHIS2 for health service reporting in 2024. The World Bank counted 69 public health facilities reporting data in DHIS2 at 31 August 2024, against a target of 80 by December 2025. WHO Comoros gives the 91 structures reached in 2025 as 100% of all public-level structures.

Not held. Nothing held says where DHIS2 reports are keyed or what share of primary clinics enter their own; the 99%, the 69 and the 100% count all public facilities. No tier is named, and no event dated within the last twelve months is held.

CPV.short: The national reporting system operates in every public health facility (February 2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics enter their own reports.
CPV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's terms of reference published in February 2024 name DHIS-2 as one of the three main information systems in use by the ministry, whose Health Technology, Communication and Information Office leads the digital health work.

Tiers in use. The same terms of reference state that DHIS-2 is in operation in all structures of the national health service, from the two central hospitals and four regional hospitals to health centres, health posts and basic health units. It has been implemented for routine epidemiological management since November 2018.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's terms of reference published in May 2023 state that DHIS2, used to manage aggregated data, is in production in all structures of the national health service and for all public health programmes.

Last twelve months. As at February 2024 DHIS-2 managed aggregated health information, mainly for epidemiological surveillance.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The February 2024 terms of reference list 32 health centres, 34 health posts and 114 basic health units among the structures in which DHIS-2 is in operation.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and nothing held says who keys them. Nothing on the system is dated after February 2024, and no plan or financing is stated for it.

DJI.short: 84% of all health facilities entered their own data in June 2025; it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
DJI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. UNFPA Djibouti states that the Ministry of Health ensures national governance of the integrated DHIS2 and GBVIMS-Health platform, which its Health Information Directorate administers, at a workshop dated 2 February 2025. The ministry began integrating gender-based violence data into what UNFPA calls the National Health Information System (DHIS2) with UNFPA's technical and financial support. The national health development plan for 2020 to 2024 committed to implementing DHIS2 across the whole national territory.

Tiers in use. WHO's country office, on 14 April 2025, listed the review and enhancement of DHIS2 as implemented at primary health care level as an action in progress.

Where data is digitised. The World Bank states that at 30 June 2025 some health facilities use DHIS-2 directly while others track data on paper and submit it immediately.

Last twelve months. The World Bank's results table shows the share of facilities with DHIS-2 data entry at the facility level rising from 69% at 31 December 2024 to 84% at 30 June 2025.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The World Bank records 84% of all health facilities with DHIS-2 data entry at the facility level at 30 June 2025, against an end target of 65% for May 2027. Its baseline was 35% in May 2022.

Not held. No current plan naming the system and no domestic budget line dated within the last three years is held. The 84% is of all health facilities, with no numerator or denominator, and no dated event in the last twelve months is held.

DZA.short: The ministry began training staff on the national reporting system in December 2023, starting with a team of 20; nothing yet shows it in use.
DZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health, with WHO support, began training health practitioners and IT staff to use the DHIS2 platform, adapted to the national context, the WHO Algeria office reports. The national digital health strategy under which the training began was still a draft in November 2023, when a pre-validation workshop of sixty participants worked on it ahead of its submission to the national authorities.

Tiers in use. The training is meant, the WHO office states, to make the national health information system yield information for decision-makers at every level.

Where data is digitised. The first session, five days in December 2023 led by an international expert, taught its participants to use the platform.

Last twelve months. The WHO office reports that further training sessions were to be programmed in the 2024-2025 work plan.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The first session trained a first team of 20 health practitioners and IT staff.

Not held. Nothing held says which tiers report through the platform, where data is keyed, how many primary clinics enter their own reports or how it is financed. No use of the platform after the first training is held.

EGY.short: Births and deaths are entered at district level into the national health information system (2025); routine clinic reporting is not shown.
EGY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Egypt's answers to the WHO EMRO civil registration questionnaire, published in 2025, describe the Ministry of Health's national health information system, into which birth and death notifications are processed.

Tiers in use. On those answers, notifications of births and deaths made at health offices go as copies to the health department at district level, and are then reviewed at directorate and central level.

Where data is digitised. The district health department processes the notifications electronically into the national system, on the answers published in 2025; the health offices below it send copies. From the directorates to the central level the work is electronic.

Last twelve months. The answers published in 2025 state that automation of the health offices is under implementation.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The same answers report a pilot of electronic registration at health-office level in some governorates, the level at which births and deaths are first notified.

Not held. Nothing held shows clinics' routine reports of patients treated entering the system: the one source describes birth and death notifications only, and the latest year it cites is 2011. No tier, clinic share, financing or event in the last twelve months is held.

ERI.short: Reports are entered at zone and sub-zone offices (2024); no primary clinic is shown entering its own.
ERI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health implemented DHIS2 as its health information system, installed on the ministry's own local area networks, with HISP Tanzania supporting customisation, upgrades and training, as a DHIS2 Community post of March 2024 described it. The ministry's sector plan, HSSDP III, covers 2022 to 2026 and treats the HMIS and DHIS2 in its Data and Information section. It places what it calls the National Health Information System under the Minister's Office, with HMIS, ICT and System Development units.

Tiers in use. HSSDP III, dated October 2021, states that DHIS2 had been rolled out to about 40 per cent of facilities at secondary level and above.

Where data is digitised. WHO Eritrea states that by 2019 DHIS 2 was installed and rolled out in all zobas, the regional level, in its offline version. In 2022 it reported a functional DHIS-2 at national level, at sub-national level and in 44% of the districts. A DHIS2 Community post of March 2024 states that data enters the national DHIS2 from zones and sub-zones over the ministry's local networks, running offline.

Last twelve months. WHO Eritrea reports that in 2022 the DHIS 2 server was upgraded to the latest version, with new data analysis and data quality applications.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. HSSDP III states that, as of October 2021, data is collected from all health facilities through paper and electronic channels.

Not held. Nothing held shows a primary clinic entering its own reports, and no share or count of clinics is held. How the system is financed is not stated, and no event dated within the last twelve months is held.

ETH.short: Hospitals and health centres enter their own reports into the national system (2024); it is not known whether health posts do.
ETH.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health holds full ownership of DHIS2's customisation and implementation, as assessed in June 2022, under a budgeted health information strategy and a 10-year strategic plan. The memorandum Ethiopia signed with the United States on 23 December 2025 names DHIS2 as the country's HMIS, and the United States plans US$18,850,149 of data-systems funding over 2026 to 2030, across all the systems it lists.

Tiers in use. In facility surveys of 2019 and 2020, 305 public hospitals and health centres reported a functional HMIS, and health posts have none of their own. The Ministry of Health counted more than 33,000 health facilities on DHIS2 in 2024.

Where data is digitised. Health information technicians key routine reports into DHIS2 at their own facilities, on interviews held from October 2023 to March 2024. Health posts record largely on paper and send monthly to their health centre, which compiles and submits, as surveyed in 2019 and 2020.

Last twelve months. The share of expected monthly facility reports received in DHIS2 rose from 90% in 2024 to 93% in 2025, on Countdown to 2030's figures.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. A study published in May 2023 states that more than 95% of all health facilities used DHIS-2, online or offline. A 2025 study puts over 4,000 primary health care institutions, 95% of those eligible, on DHIS2, counting district hospitals, health centres, health posts and district health offices.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held: both 95% figures count all or eligible health facilities, not primary clinics. Nothing dated after 2020 shows health posts entering their own data, and no exchange between eCHIS and DHIS2 is established.

GAB.short: The national system was launched in December 2024, with 122 data managers trained across 51 health departments; clinics are not shown entering their own reports.
GAB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Decree 0292/PR/MS of 21 July 2024 charges the Ministry of Health's planning directorate-general with collecting, processing and disseminating health information nationwide. The national health development plan adopted on 23 February 2024 sets a DHIS2 platform integrating all health programmes for the end of December 2028, and costs its health information axis at 3,509,631,187 FCFA. DHIS2 was launched nationally on 6 December 2024 with financial and technical support from WHO Gabon and the Global Fund, as HISP Rwanda reported.

Tiers in use. WHO Gabon states that at its December 2024 launch DHIS2 integrated all functional public health facilities, with private facilities to follow in 2025.

Where data is digitised. WHO Gabon reports that those trained to use DHIS2 in 2024 were 122 data managers and 10 regional health directors, from all 51 health departments and 10 regions.

Last twelve months. WHO Gabon directed its 2025 support to data quality, reporting completeness and timeliness, training more than 76 professionals.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The 2024-2028 plan provides for training data managers at the three levels of the health pyramid.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and no source names the tiers that report. The published completeness figures disagree, and no dated event in the last twelve months is held.

GHA.short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national system, and some community health posts enter their own (2024); how many is not published.
GHA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ghana Health Service's Policy, Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Division owns DHIMS2, the service's District Health Information Management System, which runs on a national scale, on the mapping GIZ published with the service in December 2023. The Ministry of Health's Health Information System Strategic Plan 2022-2025, of June 2022, budgets GHS 31,354,750, of which GHS 28,219,275 is from development partners. The service's Policy and Strategy on Digital Health 2023-2027 lists DHIMS II first among its digital health solutions.

Tiers in use. Community health officers in 86 CHPS zones across six Northern Region districts reported monthly into DHIMS 2 at CHPS level, in a PLOS One survey of March 2024.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's plan of June 2022 states that most facilities validate and enter their data into DHIMS2 themselves, while those without computers or internet submit manually to the sub-district for entry. CHPS staff in Karaga, Mion and Sagnarigu said in March 2024 that their compounds lacked login details and computers, and that paper reports went to the sub-district or the district office for upload.

Last twelve months. The donor-funded projects that paid for the servers hosting DHIMS2 had ended by December 2023, leaving the annual server costs unfunded.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. A WHO-led study found no electronic data collection in any of the 16 public primary facilities it visited in four districts of Ghana in 2016-2017.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the one figure on clinics is from 16 facilities in 2016-2017. No plan dated within the last three years is held, and no dated event on DHIMS2 in the last twelve months.

GIN.short: All levels reported into the national system in early 2026, with clinics' paper reports entered at district offices.
GIN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene's Bureau de Stratégie et de Développement runs the national health information system (SNIS) and DHIS2 Guinée and publishes the quarterly SNIS bulletin, on its performance bulletin for the first quarter of 2026. The bulletin places the SNIS under strategic orientation 3 of the PNDS 2025-2034 and lists GFF/R4D as the partner supporting DHIS2 in that quarter.

Tiers in use. The ministry reports that in the first quarter of 2026 all regions and all levels of the health pyramid transmitted their data on time, with national completeness at 100% and promptness at 99%.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's PASA2 programme page, published in 2025, states that health posts, health centres and prefectural hospitals collect SNIS data on paper primary tools, which are keyed into DHIS2. A CSEA policy brief of November 2025 states that weak rural connectivity forces local health centres to rely on manual reporting and paper records.

Last twelve months. In the first quarter of 2026 the SNIS reached what the ministry calls a historic record of 100% completeness, WASH indicators were integrated into DHIS2 and prefectural DHIS2 dashboards were in development.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry's statistical yearbook for 2021 says that the monthly reports of first-level health centres and improved health centres were either entered in DHIS2 or sent to the district team for entry.

Not held. No share or count of health centres or health posts entering their own reports is held; the 100% completeness is data transmitted. No domestic budget line for the SNIS is named.

GMB.short: Clinics reported on paper, and regional health offices entered the figures into the national reporting system, in 2024.
GMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's National Health Sector Policy 2021-2030, published in February 2024, calls DHIS2 the central reporting system for all national health information and puts the HMIS programme under the ministry's Directorate of Planning and Information. The policy sets the strategy of migrating fully from paper recording to a computerised system at all levels and lists a costed strategic plan for 2021-2025 as its implementing document.

Tiers in use. The policy places the electronic HMIS at the seven regional health directorates and the ministry. The ministry's service statistics report for 2021, drawn from DHIS2, carries data from referral hospitals, community clinics and the village health service.

Where data is digitised. The policy states that the HMIS is paper at the facility, in registers and monthly return forms, and electronic at the regional health directorates and the centre. From 1 October 2023 one secondary-level hospital, Bundung Maternal and Child Health Hospital, had its monthly indicators integrated into DHIS2 automatically from scanned forms, in a pilot.

Last twelve months. Between June and November 2024 the 11 sites of a tuberculosis pilot kept generating their monthly reports for the DHIS2 aggregate system from paper registers.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The policy gives electronic entry only at the regional health directorates and centrally. A World Bank assessment of July 2023 states that many lower-level facilities continue to collect HMIS data on paper.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is published, and no dated event falls in the twelve months to 30 September 2026. No statement of who finances the HMIS is held from the last three years.

GNB.short: Health centres' paper reports were entered into the national system at 11 health directorates (June 2023); how many clinics enter their own is not published.
GNB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The DHIS2 project's country profile, updated July 2026, describes Guinea-Bissau's DHIS2 systems as locally owned, with the Ministry of Health leading the work on them with Saudigitus (HISP Mozambique). The Ministry of Public Health's PNDS III, of June 2023, places the national health information system, the SNIS, under INASA and names a strategic plan for it, PENSIS 2022-2026. Support agreed in October 2026 is coordinated by UNDP and paid for by the Global Fund.

Tiers in use. INASA's health statistics yearbook for 2022 tabulates the monthly reports of health centres entered in DHIS2: 1,747 of 2,073 expected reports were entered, a completeness of 82.2 per cent.

Where data is digitised. PNDS III, of June 2023, states that all the SNIS paper forms and reports are digitised in the 11 health directorates, on the DHIS2 platform.

Last twelve months. On 22 December 2025 the DHIS2 project announced that the HISP network, selected by the Global Fund, will give technical assistance to seven African countries including Guinea-Bissau to integrate climate data into their national HMIS. On 6 October 2026 it announced an agreement to support INASA on the national system's data quality, with new tools to track patients with HIV or tuberculosis.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. INASA reported in January 2019 that tablet entry of data directly from the health areas entered a pilot phase in 2018. The 2022 yearbook gives the public network as 111 type C, 19 type B and 5 type A health centres.

Not held. No number or share of health centres keying their own reports is published, and no later fact follows the 2018 tablet pilot. No coverage fact is dated after June 2023, and no domestic budget line for the system is stated.

GNQ.short: The national reporting system was piloted in two districts, Baney and Añisok, in 2025; a planned national expansion in 2026 is not confirmed.
GNQ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry announced the conclusion of the DHIS2 pilot on 25 November 2025 and presents the platform as its tool for the national health system. It states that the pilot ran under a primary-care agreement financed by the Spanish cooperation agency AECID. UNDP, on 1 March 2025, quotes the health minister placing the digitalisation within the national health development plan PNDS 2021-2025.

Tiers in use. EHAS states that the first pilot, in 2025, let health facilities in two districts, insular Baney and continental Añisok, enter real data.

Where data is digitised. EHAS, in 2025, states that health facilities filled paper register sheets, which ministry staff periodically collected and transferred to spreadsheets. In the Baney and Añisok pilot data is entered from the health facility with the DHIS2 Android or web app where digital means are available, and at the District Office otherwise.

Last twelve months. On 25 November 2025 the ministry declared the pilot in Baney and Añisok successfully completed and said it would be the reference for a national expansion of DHIS2 foreseen for 2026.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry states that the DHIS2 pilot ran in 2025 in two health districts, Baney and Añisok, with 104 health professionals trained.

Not held. No source names the tiers or counts the facilities entering data in the Baney and Añisok pilot, and nothing dated after November 2025 shows the national expansion foreseen for 2026 under way. No plan naming DHIS2 and no domestic budget line dated within the last three years is held.

KEN.short: Facilities across the country enter their reports online into the national system (2024), but no figure shows how many primary clinics do so themselves.
KEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health uses the Kenya Health Information System (KHIS) to collect health data from facilities nationwide, as IDinsight reported in October 2024. The ministry's strategic plan for July 2023 to June 2027 takes most of its indicator baselines and targets from KHIS. USAID's HealthIT grant committed US$22,528,318 over 2016 to 2021 to DHIS2 implementation and use.

Tiers in use. KHIS Aggregate collects data from health facilities nationwide and is designed for every level of the health system, from the national down to the community, as IDinsight described it in October 2024.

Where data is digitised. Facilities record services in paper daily registers, summarise them at the end of the week or month, and enter and submit the summaries online in KHIS, on IDinsight's account of October 2024.

Last twelve months. Legal Notice 77 of 2025, in force from 11 April 2025, made the Digital Health Agency responsible for maintaining the Health Management Information Services Platform for reporting.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Ministry of Health's mid-term review reports that 94% of all health facilities submitted reports within KHIS in 2019/20, up from 89% in 2017/18.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 94% is a reporting rate. No financing for KHIS dated within the last three years is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months.

LBR.short: All facilities report monthly into the national system (2024), with district and county clerks entering the figures from paper forms (2022).
LBR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's report for 2024 states that its HMIS runs on DHIS2 and is managed within its Department of Policy, Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation. The ministry's Data Quality Improvement Plan of June 2022 runs 2022 to 2026 and is costed at US$7,312,887.50. The memorandum signed with the United States on 9 December 2025 plans US$1,338,372 of US funding for HMIS/DHIS2 over 2026 to 2030.

Tiers in use. Every health facility, public and private, is required to report service data monthly, and counties submit to the central ministry by the 17th of the following month, on the ministry's account for 2024.

Where data is digitised. Evidence Action's survey found that all 48 facilities surveyed in Montserrado, Margibi and Grand Bassa filled paper HMIS forms monthly, which district or county data clerks entered into DHIS2, in records for May to July 2022. The Liberian team's Countdown to 2030 synthesis of June 2022 says facilities' monthly reports are normally collected by the County Health Team for entry into DHIS2.

Last twelve months. WHO reports that in 2025, with Gavi support, it delivered 31 laptops with statistical software for data analysis in the health management information and surveillance systems.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Countdown to 2030 synthesis counts 856 functional health facilities submitting reports through DHIS2, of 964 on the Master Facility List, for data of January 2017 to December 2021.

Not held. No national figure for clinics entering their own reports is held. Nothing on where data is keyed is dated after July 2022, and no event dated inside the last twelve months is held.

LBY.short: The national system was rolled out to 465 primary care facilities and 51 hospitals in 2023; how many clinics enter their own reports is unknown.
LBY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's Health Information Centre gives technical support to the DHIS2 platform, as WHO described it in 2024. WHO states that all health information system activities in 2024 followed the 2024-2025 HIS operational plan. The 2023 rollout was enabled by WHO with UNICEF, IOM, GIZ, the International Rescue Committee, the International Medical Corps and UNFPA.

Tiers in use. WHO states that in 2023 it and the ministry rolled out DHIS2 in 40 municipalities, covering 465 primary health care facilities and 51 hospitals.

Where data is digitised. WHO states that 655 health staff from public primary health care facilities, hospitals and municipal health administration were trained on DHIS2 in 2023 and given laptops, desktops and tablets to enable data entry. In December 2024 WHO and the ministry visited five health facilities in Suq Aljuma municipality, Tripoli, to assess their DHIS2 data entry compliance and the timeliness and completeness of their reporting.

Last twelve months. Libya Review reported on 7 November 2025 a meeting of the ministry and WHO that explored the feasibility of extending DHIS2 to pharmacy management, supply forecasting and service monitoring in public facilities.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. WHO counts 465 primary health care facilities among the 516 facilities where DHIS2 was rolled out in 2023. WHO also states that DHIS2 reached 100% national geographic coverage by March 2023 and that consistent reporting from health facilities remains a challenge.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held: the 465 are facilities where DHIS2 was rolled out, with no denominator. The sources name hospitals and primary health care facilities, not their levels, and nothing held shows the operational plan running beyond 2025 or financing dated after 2023.

LSO.short: 231 facilities report HIV figures into the national system (2025); clinics entering their own data is shown only in four pilot districts, up to 2017.
LSO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's Health Management Information System has run on DHIS2 since February 2015, and an officer of its HMIS Division presented how health data is collected from communities and facilities at a workshop reported on 23 September 2026. In 2025 Lesotho endorsed its National Digital Health Strategy 2025-2030, WHO's country office reports.

Tiers in use. A BMJ Open study covers monthly routine reporting by 60 health centres and 6 hospitals in the four pilot districts of Berea, Butha Buthe, Leribe and Mohale's Hoek over July 2013 to June 2017.

Where data is digitised. Under the primary health care reform pilot of July 2014 to June 2017, each health facility nurse in charge was given a computer and submitted the monthly report from the facility, while the registers stayed on paper. In November 2025 the ministry's HIV programme stated that facility reports are automated from its electronic medical record into DHIS2.

Last twelve months. WHO's country office reports that during 2025 Lesotho advanced interoperability across its HMIS, HRH, LMIS and surveillance platforms. The HIV programme states that 231 facilities report on HIV indicators and that reporting rates fell from 97% in January to 95% in September 2025.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The four pilot districts where facilities submitted monthly reports electronically held 66 facilities, 60 health centres and 6 hospitals, and about 40% of the population, out of 10 districts, to June 2017.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and how facilities without the electronic medical record enter theirs is not stated. Nothing on tiers or clinics is dated after 2017, and no financing within the last three years is held.

MAR.short: A national reporting system was working in every public health centre by December 2019; no figure shows how many centres enter their own reports.
MAR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Health Compact of 6 December 2025 makes the Ministry of Health and Social Protection and the territorial health groups accountable for deploying an integrated health information system, which it calls the SIIS, in all primary health care establishments and all university hospitals. The World Bank ties US$37.5 million of its US$450 million loan to health data, with nothing disbursed against it at 20 June 2025.

Tiers in use. The World Bank's report of June 2025 gives as its baseline that an integrated and digitalised health information system was deployed at hospitals and that deployment had begun in primary health care centres. The World Bank reports an earlier system, which the ministry calls the SMIPF-SC, operational in public health centres in all regions by December 2019.

Where data is digitised. The SMIPF-SC gave service-utilisation data at facility level by December 2019, aggregated through dashboards at provincial, regional and central levels, the World Bank reports. Results data came from a paper-based system until the SMIPF-SC supplied them from 2018.

Last twelve months. The Compact gives the SIIS, at 6 December 2025, as being deployed in primary health care establishments and in progress in university hospitals.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The World Bank's completion report gives the SMIPF-SC as operational in 100% of public health centres by December 2019. Its report of June 2025 has deployment of the integrated system begun in primary health care centres.

Not held. No share or count of health centres entering their own reports is held, and no source says who keys the data; the 100% is of centres where the system was operational, in 2019. No domestic budget line for the system is named.

MDG.short: Health centres in all 114 districts report into the national system, with district offices entering their paper forms (2023).
MDG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's plan for its health information system, the PSRSIS, assigns routine data to the ministry's DEPSI directorate and records that the ministry adopted DHIS2 as its data warehouse under the 2018-2022 plan. The plan runs from 2023 to 2027, carries a costed budget by strategy and names DHIS2 throughout.

Tiers in use. The plan states that DHIS2 was scaled to all 22 regions and 114 districts in January 2019 for the basic health centres' monthly activity report, and that the district hospitals' and community reports were integrated from July 2020. What the plan calls the CHU/CHRR/ES report was last updated in 2011, and DHIS2 is only to be brought forward for it.

Where data is digitised. As at the 2023 plan, the basic health centres' data go up to the districts on the integrated monthly report in paper form, which is keyed into the DHIS2 Routine platform.

Last twelve months. WHO Madagascar lists among the key actions of 2024-2025 an audit of the DHIS2 platform and secured cloud hosting, the deployment of electronic registers including the monthly activity report, and the distribution of tablets with DHIS2 training.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The 2023 plan states that an electronic monthly report keyed directly at health facilities has been piloted since 2021 and is available in 10 pilot districts, with scale-up being planned.

Not held. No count or share of basic health centres keying their own monthly report is held, for the pilot districts or for the electronic registers deployed in 2024-2025. No financing statement dated within the last three years is held, and no event dated within the last twelve months.

MLI.short: Community and referral health centres and hospitals had routine data in the national system in 2019; how many clinics enter their own is not known.
MLI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The DHIS2 platform is coordinated by a technical team and a steering committee chaired by the Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development, by the ministry's plan of February 2021, which records no budget line for the national health information system. The digital health plan for 2024 to 2028 bases that system on DHIS2 and schedules a DHIS2 test server and an interoperability framework.

Tiers in use. Since 2016 the routine data of community health centres (CSCom), reference health centres (CSRéf) and hospitals has been on the DHIS2 platform, the same plan states, with figures for 2019.

Where data is digitised. In four sub-districts of Mopti in September and October 2018, the technical director of each CSCom entered community health workers' paper monthly reports into DHIS2, the Population Council found. The ministry's agency ANTIM places mobile terminals carrying a form at CSCom and CSRéf for its SNISI platform, by the platform's own page as read on 3 September 2026.

Last twelve months. At a workshop of 30 and 31 July 2025 the ministry's Directorate General of Health and Public Hygiene reviewed community indicators for alignment with DHIS2, and a deputy director said interoperability between DHIS2 and DISC-Mali was established, Muso reports.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. By September 2019 the health ministry had deployed DHIS-2 in 98 percent of community health centers, USAID's assessment of April 2023 states.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 98% is a deployment share. Tiers and coverage are not dated since 2019, no financing within the last three years is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months.

MOZ.short: District health offices entered facilities' monthly paper forms into the national system in 2019; nothing more recent is held.
MOZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's own page states that its Departamento de Informação para Saúde manages SIS-MA, the ministry's aggregate health information system. The ministry's Plano de Melhoria de Qualidade de Dados 2025-2029, dated January 2025, is a national plan for the quality of data in SIS-MA.

Tiers in use. A 2019 assessment by the University of Oslo, Eduardo Mondlane University and the ministry found that SISMA's users, services and health facilities were registered and configured centrally at the ministry, with support passing from district and provincial statisticians to its technical teams.

Where data is digitised. The same assessment, covering 14 districts, found that facilities' monthly data reached the district health office on paper forms and were entered into SISMA there. A study led with the ministry found in 2016-17 that public primary care facilities submitted monthly paper forms to the district management office, where the data were entered.

Last twelve months. The data quality plan of January 2025 followed the ministry's 2022-23 assessment of 175 facilities in all 11 provinces, which found that only 9% of records matched exactly between facility registers and SIS-MA.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. None of the 16 randomly selected public primary care facilities visited in four districts had electronic data collection in place in 2016-17, the study led with the ministry reports.

Not held. No coverage fact is dated after 2019. Which tiers use SIS-MA, how many primary clinics enter their own reports, financing within the last three years and any dated event in the last twelve months are not held.

MRT.short: District offices enter health posts' paper reports into the national system (2023); no figure shows how many clinics enter their own.
MRT.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Arrêté n° 1496 of 14 December 2021 assigns collection and analysis of data for the SNIS, the Ministry of Health's name for its information system, to its regional and circonscription services. The ministry's PNDS 2021-2030 commits to a SNIS strategic plan to 2030 and requires all its indicators to be included in DHIS2. The European Commission's 2025 action document for PASS IV sets aside EUR 3,000,000 for interoperable government-owned digital solutions, the information system among them.

Tiers in use. The World Bank's PHCPI assessment, published in 2023, states that health posts and health centres collect SNIS data and send them to the moughataa health centre, across all health districts. A ministry and Countdown to 2030 analysis of June 2025 states that, for institutional mortality, only the hospitals of Hodh Gharbi and Guidimagha have data integrated in DHIS2.

Where data is digitised. The World Bank assessment states that health posts report on paper to health centres, where the information is made digital, and DHIS2 takes the districts' data. Article 18 of the 2021 arrêté charges the circonscription sanitaire's service with entering its health statistics reports into the database.

Last twelve months. Countdown to 2030 reports that from 3 to 7 November 2025 a national workshop trained district-level focal points to use routine SNIS data, with practical sessions in DHIS2.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The World Bank's 2023 assessment gives a coverage rate of 92 percent for monthly summary reports from basic health facilities.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held; the 92 percent is report coverage, given without a numerator or denominator. Nothing held shows a health post entering its own data, or hospitals beyond the two named integrated.

MUS.short: In January 2022 the national system was used only at regional and national level, with entry by clinics still planned; nothing more recent is held.
MUS.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. DHIS2's own country story of January 2022 states that the government, through the Ministry of Health and Wellness, has begun implementing DHIS2 as the national health information system, the work done by the health ministry and the Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation with support from WHO, Gavi, the Global Fund, HISP UiO and HISP Uganda. The implementation is carried out under the Health Sector Strategic Plan 2020-2024.

Tiers in use. In January 2022 DHIS2 was in use at regional and national level, on the same account.

Where data is digitised. WHO's SCORE assessment, on data from 2013 to 2018, rates a standardised system of electronic data entry for aggregate reporting at district or comparable level as 'not there', and completeness of reporting above 75% for public primary care facilities, public hospitals and private facilities. The ministry's strategic plan of 2020 states that the health information system in Rodrigues is largely manual.

Last twelve months. Decentralising DHIS2 further will need more training, staff and IT infrastructure, the story of January 2022 states.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. In January 2022 the health authorities planned to decentralise DHIS2 to district and primary health care level, and to Rodrigues and Agalega.

Not held. Nothing on the HMIS dated after January 2022 is held, so whether the planned decentralisation to district and primary level has happened is not established. Nor is which tiers use DHIS2 routinely, or whether it carries routine reporting of patients treated.

MWI.short: District offices enter paper reports from 1,266 facilities into the national system (2023); how many health centres enter their own is not published.
MWI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health has collected aggregated facility data since 2002 through a unified HMIS under its Central Monitoring and Evaluation Division, which runs on DHIS2, on a study published in December 2024. The Global Fund's Inspector General reported in late 2023 that the Fund had invested US$21 million in the system since Grant Cycle 4.

Tiers in use. As of January 2023, 1,266 health facilities, government-owned and private, were reporting in the HMIS on DHIS2. Countdown to 2030, with the ministry, puts completeness of monthly facility reporting in DHIS2 at 97% of expected reports nationally in 2025, up from 83% in 2020.

Where data is digitised. An August 2023 survey of six facilities and three district health offices found that facilities compile monthly reports on paper and deliver them to the district health office, where the data are entered on computer. A study published in December 2024 states that paper forms are compiled at facilities and entered into DHIS2 at the district HMIS office.

Last twelve months. A project that began in December 2025 and runs to March 2027 will deploy DHIS2 climate and health tools on the national HMIS, first in four districts.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The ministry states that expanding DHIS2 Mobile to the 24 remaining districts in 2023 allows direct data entry into DHIS2 by all health centres. Neno district began moving DHIS2 data entry to its health centres in November 2022.

Not held. No count or share of health centres entering their own reports is published, and whether health centres key their reports in practice is not established. No current plan naming the system is held.

NAM.short: Clinics report on paper, and district officers enter their monthly forms into the national reporting system (2026 study).
NAM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Managers interviewed for a study published in March 2026 said that the Ministry of Health and Social Services manages DHIS2 centrally, on a server at headquarters where national staff alone change its design, add indicators and run backups. They said that external donors pay for customising DHIS2, fund the training and buy the computers. Namibia launched a National Digital Health Policy for 2026 to 2036, a ten-year framework to strengthen health information systems, in February 2026 on WHO's account.

Tiers in use. The same managers said that DHIS2 is used at district, regional and national levels.

Where data is digitised. District HIS officers key the monthly paper summary forms sent in by health facilities into the DHIS2 aggregate module at the district office, on the managers' account of March 2026.

Last twelve months. The Ministry of Health and Social Services launched the National Digital Health Policy (2026-2036) in February 2026, which WHO says is to address fragmentation across health information systems.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The health minister told the National Assembly on 6 May 2025 that health data collection had expanded to over 90 clinics beyond district and hospital levels. The managers said in the study of March 2026 that primary health facilities still report on paper tools.

Not held. Which tiers use DHIS2 is not established, and no share of primary clinics entering their own reports is published: the count of over 90 clinics comes with no total. Nothing in the last twelve months changes where reports are entered.

NER.short: A 2023 ministry guide has health centres enter their monthly reports into the national system; no figure shows how many do.
NER.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The health ministry's monitoring guide of December 2023 makes its Direction des Statistiques responsible at central level for the monthly reports of the Système National d'Information Sanitaire (SNIS). The guide, written for the health development plan 2022-2026, names DHIS2 as the base for managing routine health data. The e-health strategy of 2019 planned USD 1.00 million of the SNIS project's USD 1.20 million from partners and nothing from the ministry.

Tiers in use. The guide has every health establishment key its monthly report into DHIS2, naming integrated health centres (CSI) and hospitals as data sources. Health posts send their data to their CSI by the 10th, where it is checked and keyed.

Where data is digitised. The circuit the guide sets in December 2023 is that each establishment fills a standard monthly activity report, validates it and keys it into DHIS2, the CSI by the 15th of the following month. DHIS2 has been online since September 2016.

Last twelve months. The guide of December 2023 sets yearly targets to 2026 for the timeliness and completeness of SNIS reports.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The guide gives, from the 2021 statistical yearbook, a CSI report completeness rate of 97.90% and a timeliness rate of 54.63% for 2021, as reports transmitted over reports expected. In September 2018 the ministry counted 1,026 integrated health centres and 2,443 health huts in the public network.

Not held. No count or share of integrated health centres keying their own reports into DHIS2 is held; the 2021 rates measure reports transmitted. No financing dated within the last three years is held, no dated event in the last twelve months, and no community system is shown exchanging data with the SNIS.

NGA.short: 91.5% of all health facilities reported into the national system in June 2025, with local government offices entering the figures from paper.
NGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Federal Ministry of Health issues the monthly bulletin of the National Health Management Information System (NHMIS), and its annual report for 2021 places the single national DHIS2 instance in the ministry's Department of Health Planning, Research and Statistics. In the health memorandum signed with the United States on 19 December 2025, Nigeria commits to use DHIS2 as its national health data warehouse, and the United States plans to fund it over 2026-2030.

Tiers in use. The ministry's bulletin gives the national health facility reporting rate for the NHMIS monthly summary on DHIS-2 as 91.5% for June 2025, and charts the rate for primary, secondary and tertiary facilities, public and private.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's annual report for 2021 has facilities submit a paper monthly summary form to the LGA office by the 7th, where it is entered into DHIS2 by the 14th. Gavi's Zero-Dose Learning Hub assessment, published in November 2024, states that monthly reports are entered manually into DHIS2 at LGA offices. In June 2025 the ministry encouraged states to deploy mobile devices and computers for direct reporting to DHIS-2.

Last twelve months. The memorandum of 19 December 2025 expects DHIS2 to collect and report all of its outcome and process metrics.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. A WHO-led study found that none of the 16 randomly selected public primary health care facilities it visited in Nigeria in 2016-2017 had electronic data collection.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and the 2016-2017 sample does not carry the country. No dated event in the last twelve months is held, and Nigeria's own commitment to data systems is not broken down to DHIS2.

RWA.short: Every health facility enters its own reports (audit to 2023); it stays at stage 3 because no current plan or budget was found.
RWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health upgraded the HMIS, established in 1998, to web-based DHIS2 from 2012. The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda describes the system in 2025 as operating countrywide under the ministry's management.

Tiers in use. The Global Fund's Inspector General states, for the period to December 2023, that DHIS2 has been rolled out at all health facilities, a network of referral, provincial and district hospitals, 505 health centres and 1,250 health posts. The ministry's booklet for fiscal year 2023/24 reports HMIS counts by facility level for referral, provincial and district hospitals, medicalized health centres and medical clinics.

Where data is digitised. Data is reported into DHIS2 at the health facilities, after monthly validation meetings led by the heads of facilities, on the Inspector General's account of the period to December 2023. In 2017 heads of service filled paper forms from registers and the facility's own data manager uploaded the data into DHIS2 by the 5th of the month.

Last twelve months. The National Institute of Statistics describes the system as it stood in 2025 as still capturing aggregated births and deaths to check the civil registration system.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Inspector General states that DHIS2 is rolled out at all health facilities, in the audit covering July 2021 to December 2023. Authors at the University of Rwanda and the Rwanda Biomedical Center held HMIS immunisation reports for October to December 2022 for all 520 primary health facilities.

Not held. No plan or financing for the HMIS dated within the last three years is held, and no dated event in the last twelve months. No measured share of clinics entering their own reports is held, and whether the health posts key theirs is not established.

SDN.short: Local health offices entered facilities' reports into the system in 144 of 189 localities in 2020; nothing since April 2023 shows where data is entered.
SDN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Federal Ministry of Health established an integrated health management information system in 2013 and deployed DHIS2 from 2016, WHO's 2020 assessment records. Its strategic plan for 2022-2024 names DHIS2 in three strategic interventions. Participants at the ministry's review meeting of February 2026 recommended continued technical and financial support from partners, the Global Fund and UNICEF among them.

Tiers in use. WHO's 2020 assessment states that DHIS2 had not been implemented in most hospitals. The ministry's plan gives 86.40 per cent of selected hospitals as using DHIS2 in 2021.

Where data is digitised. WHO's 2020 assessment states that facility data are entered into DHIS2 at the locality level, and that the platform covered 144 of 189 localities in 17 states, of which 122 reported in May 2020.

Last twelve months. The Federal Minister of Health told the 2025 annual health information performance review that data reporting coverage rose from 13 per cent at the onset of the crisis to more than 56 per cent by the end of 2025. At that meeting, in February 2026, its Director General of Health Information called for a full transition from paper-based to digital reporting through DHIS2.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The Global Fund's Inspector General found in 2018 that DHIS2 was not used in health facilities, their results being consolidated on paper and keyed above them. The ministry's plan gives the DHIS2 reporting rate at primary health care level as 46.90 per cent in 2021.

Not held. Nothing dated after April 2023 says where data is keyed, which localities still enter it or whether any facility enters its own reports. The 56 per cent has no numerator or denominator, and whether hospitals key their own reports is not established.

SEN.short: The national system is used at every level, with figures entered from the district upwards (2021); how many clinics enter their own is unknown.
SEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministère de la Santé et de l'Action sociale has run the DHIS2 implementation since 2013, on a DHIS2 Community post of 2 March 2021. The ministry's sector policy letter of 25 March 2025 states that a national strategic plan 2022-2026 for the health and social information system is in force. The NGO PATH contributes technical and financial assistance.

Tiers in use. DHIS2 was scaled nationally between 2015 and 2016 and is used at all levels of the health pyramid: hospitals, health centres and health posts, as the DHIS2 Community post of 2 March 2021 states.

Where data is digitised. The ministry's IT master plan of 31 December 2021 states that DHIS2 runs from the health districts up to the minister's cabinet. In the Thiès, Mbour, Kédougou and Saraya districts in 2018, health-post head nurses entered monthly reports drawn from paper registers into DHIS2, on a BMC Public Health study.

Last twelve months. The World Bank's programme document of 11 December 2025 states that health worker strikes over the past 2.5 years have left gaps in data collection, storage and reporting across DHIS2. The national malaria programme put national completeness of the data entered in DHIS2 for 2023 at 26.66%, against 97.8% in 2021.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The DHIS2 Community post of 2 March 2021 states that DHIS2 is used in health centres and health posts for data entry and analysis.

Not held. No share or count of primary clinics entering their own reports is held, and no coverage fact is dated after 2021. No approved financing for the system dated within the last three years is held.

SLE.short: District offices enter clinics' paper reports into the national reporting system (2020 procedure, 2023 assessment).
SLE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Health's National Digital Health Roadmap 2024-2026 lists DHIS2 as the health management information system, deployed by the Ministry in all districts. The landscape assessment by GIZ and the Ministry, dated January 2023, states that its 2022 statutory budget made no provision for digital health.

Tiers in use. The January 2023 assessment states that all 34 secondary and all 10 tertiary facilities it surveyed had M&E Officers whose role was predominantly data capture and upload on DHIS2.

Where data is digitised. Under the Ministry's HMIS procedures manual of April 2020, peripheral health units compile monthly reports from paper registers and send hard copies to the District Health Management Team, where a data entry officer keys them into DHIS2, and a hospital's M&E officer enters the hospital's data. The January 2023 assessment found M&E Officers at district level capturing and uploading data on DHIS2.

Last twelve months. Statistics Sierra Leone, the Ministry of Health and APHRC give DHIS2 completeness of expected monthly facility reports as 98% nationally in 2024, with all districts at 90% or more.

Primary clinics doing the digital input. The April 2020 manual has no peripheral health unit entering its own data, and notes a plan for 2020 to move electronic entry to the community health centres.
